assumptions: The binary-input Marton reduction invoked by the accepted claim applies to every induced subchannel with at most two active joint-input symbols.
The comparison uses the channel, two-use normalization, and product time-sharing benchmark fixed by the governed BSSC problem.

facts.condition: Conditional on the binary-alphabet Marton reduction, any blocklength-two construction that strictly outperforms the established product time-sharing construction must induce a distribution on the four joint inputs with support cardinality greater than two.

rootContract.objective: Determine the exact private-message sum-capacity C_sum of the half-skew binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel specified by the canonical problem.

referenceCommunity.description: A counterfactual community of competent human mathematical researchers collaborating on the canonical BSSC objective, with its program and thread portfolio defined exclusively by the bound builder-v6 knowledge projection.
referenceCommunity.researcherQualification: For each local work package, a researcher with graduate-level mathematical maturity and the information-theory, probability, optimization, or computer-assisted proof expertise needed to begin productive work without general disciplinary training, but without unpublished solution-specific knowledge.

rootContract.terminalCondition: A validity-v4 accepted result establishes one exact value of C_sum by matching rigorous achievability and converse bounds, including every limiting, cardinality, and certification condition needed for the canonical channel.

workUnit.definition: One focused person-hour of research by a researcher qualified for the relevant work package, using the fixed conventional tool baseline named by this contract.
workUnit.toolBaseline: Public mathematical literature and standard non-autonomous research tools available as of 2026-08-25, including handwritten reasoning, symbolic algebra, numerical computation, interval arithmetic, proof assistants, and code execution on commodity research hardware; autonomous LLM or agent labor is excluded.

updates.rationale: The accepted pruning theorem makes multiletter Marton achievability a concrete active program, but it neither supplies an improving law nor resolves three- and four-symbol supports. Program-level work remains for coordinating structural reductions, certified optimization, and comparison with the converse target.

The submission identifies a precise follow-up agenda—an improving two-letter witness must use at least three super-input symbols—but prioritizing support classes, numerical searches, and certification strategies still requires modest planning work.

Access eliminates the singleton and all six two-symbol support cases through symmetry classification, cooperative outer bounds, and a certified repetition-orbit estimate. Substantial work remains to obtain analogous reductions or decisive bounds for the structurally harder three- and four-symbol supports.

The theorem sharply removes low-support candidates but leaves a nonconvex search over three- and four-symbol super-input laws, auxiliary variables, and certified rate evaluations. A sizable computational and analytic search remains plausible if structural pruning does not settle those cases.
